passage: Liam leaned on Tariq's desk in the Manchester site office. "Sign the inspection sheet for the delivery, would you? The lorry's leaving, and I'll take it from here." Tariq had not inspected it. He was still on probation, and his parents relied on his pay. His palms went damp. He thought about pretending he had no choice. Instead he said, "I'd like to check the delivery first. It will take ten minutes." Liam sighed. "You're new. Don't make trouble." That night Tariq read the staff handbook and found the section on raising concerns, and he wrote down who to speak to at the firm. The next morning he told Liam calmly he would not sign what he had not seen. The fear did not vanish, but he had chosen.

qa.q: In which city was the site office?
qa.a: The site office was in Manchester.

qa.q: What was Tariq afraid of when his palms went damp?
qa.a: He feared refusing would cost him his probation and hurt his family's income. The fear was real and understandable.

qa.q: What could Tariq do if Liam keeps pressing him?
qa.a: He can keep refusing calmly, use the raising-concerns section of the handbook, speak to the named person, and keep notes of what was asked.

qa.q: How might Liam see Tariq's refusal?
qa.a: Liam called Tariq "new" and told him not to make trouble, so Liam may see the check as a delay or a challenge. Liam may be under time pressure from the lorry leaving.

grounding: The protagonist fears refusing will cost his probation and family income, checks what protection exists and refuses calmly.

passage: People ask why I still talk about my first month at the pharmacy. I'm Rajni, and it's because of one Friday. My supervisor told me to sell a strip of antibiotics to a customer without a prescription. 'Everyone does it. If you want to pass probation, don't be difficult.' My father's shop had closed that year. My salary was the family's rent. I stood behind the counter feeling my knees go soft. I could have told myself I had no choice. That would have been easier to live with. Instead I asked for five minutes and called my senior from college, Vasudha, who now worked as a pharmacist in another city. She said, 'Check your company's rules. Most have a policy on this, and a helpline.' I found it on the staff notice board. I told the customer, calmly, that I couldn't without a prescription. My supervisor was cold for a week. I passed probation anyway. I might not have. I'd still choose it.

qa.q: What did the supervisor tell Rajni to do?
qa.a: The supervisor told Rajni to sell a strip of antibiotics without a prescription.

qa.q: What was Rajni feeling behind the counter?
qa.a: Rajni felt afraid, knees going soft, because the salary paid the family's rent.
Calling Vasudha, finding the company's policy and helpline on the notice board, and then refusing the customer calmly.

qa.q: How does Vasudha help without deciding for Rajni?
qa.a: Vasudha points Rajni to the company's rules and helpline, leaving the choice with Rajni.

grounding: A spoken account of real fear for probation and family income, and choosing to check the protections, refuse calmly and own the choice.

passage:
Tuesday: On day forty of his probation at a transport company in Nashik, Dhruv's supervisor told him to sign the load sheet for a truck he hadn't weighed. 'It's the same as always. Sign it, or I'll tell head office you're slow.' Dhruv's family had moved into a new rented flat on his salary. He went home and didn't sleep.
Thursday: He told his cousin Sabina, who worked in HR at a bank. She didn't tell him what to do. She asked, 'What does your offer letter say about safety rules? Is there a grievance email?' They found both. 'Now weigh it honestly. What really happens if you refuse? What happens if that truck is overloaded and you signed?'
Friday: Dhruv went to the weighbridge before the supervisor arrived, weighed the truck, and wrote the true figure. It was over the limit. He showed his supervisor calmly and saved the grievance email address in his phone. The truck left lighter. The supervisor didn't speak to him all day.

qa.q: On which day of his probation was Dhruv asked to sign?
qa.a: Dhruv was asked on day forty of his probation.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling on Tuesday night?
qa.a: Dhruv felt afraid and sleepless, worried that refusing would cost his probation and the family's rent.

qa.q: What steps did Dhruv take before refusing?
qa.a: He checked the safety rules and grievance email with Sabina, weighed the consequences honestly, then weighed the truck and recorded the true figure.

qa.q: How does Sabina help Dhruv think it through?
qa.a: Sabina asks questions instead of deciding for him, helping him see both the risk of refusing and the risk of signing.

grounding: Shows real fear of losing probation and family income, and Dhruv checking what protection exists, weighing the consequences and refusing calmly.
